meta.title: Anselm — The Agentic Workflow Platform That Builds Itself
meta.description: Anselm is a local-first agentic workflow platform. Describe what you need and the AI creates the functions, agents, and workflows, schedules them, and runs them durably on your own machine with SQLite, approvals, and full run history.

hero.title: The Agentic Workflow Platform That Builds Itself.
hero.lead: Describe what you need in plain language. Anselm creates the functions, agents, and workflows, schedules them, and runs them durably on your own machine. No orchestration code, no infrastructure to manage. Download, open, ask: no API key needed to start.
hero.shotAlt: Anselm desktop app showing a conversation that created a weekly digest workflow and is waiting for approval

story.title: From a Sentence to a Scheduled, Supervised Workflow.
story.lead: Every screenshot on this page comes from the same workspace and the same request: a weekly digest of a GitHub repository, reviewed by a person before it is filed.

steps.name: Describe
steps.body: Ask for the outcome in chat. Anselm plans the work, creates each building block, and reports what it built with links to every entity and run.

steps.name: Build
steps.body: The result is a real workflow: a cron trigger, a Function that calls GitHub, an Agent that writes the digest, an approval step, and a Function that files the document. All versioned.

steps.name: Schedule
steps.body: The Scheduler shows what is running, what is waiting on you, what failed in the last 24 hours, and when the next fire is due.

steps.name: Supervise
steps.body: Approvals, failures, and completions land in a durable ledger. Approve from the notification, the run continues, and the draft in the Library is published.

surfaces.title: One Desktop App. Everything the AI Builds, in View.
surfaces.lead: Chat is where work starts. The other surfaces let you inspect, schedule, supervise, and configure everything the AI built.

items.name: Chat
items.body: Where work starts. Ask, attach, mention, and watch entities appear as the conversation goes.
items.lead: A conversation is the front door to everything Anselm can build and run. Each thread keeps its own working directory, attachments, tools, and a live activity panel.

points.name: Builds while you talk
points.body: Tool cards show each Function, Agent, Trigger, and Workflow as it is created, edited, or run, with links into the entity and run pages.

points.name: Threads that live in a directory
points.body: Attach a conversation to a working directory. Branches, worktrees, and file changes stay in that thread's context.

points.name: Human in the loop
points.body: Dangerous actions wait for confirmation, questions wait for an answer, and approvals wait for a decision. State is persisted, so nothing is lost if you step away.

shots.name: chat
shots.caption: The digest workflow was built in one thread. The approval band at the top belongs to the run it started.

items.name: Entities
items.body: Every Function, Handler, Agent, and Workflow with versions, relations, and a live debug console.
items.lead: Everything the AI builds is a first-class, versioned entity. Inspect the code, the configuration, the version history, and the executions of each one.

points.name: Four kinds of building blocks
points.body: Functions run sandboxed code once. Handlers keep state across calls. Agents are LLM workers with tools and instructions. Workflows compose them into a graph.

points.name: Immutable versions, movable pointer
points.body: Every edit creates a new version. Revert is a pointer move. In-flight runs keep the versions they started with.

points.name: Relations you can see
points.body: The relationship graph shows which conversation created what, which workflow uses which Function, and which document a run produced.

shots.caption: The graph editor: three parallel fetches fan in to the digest, a Control node routes on activity, and the inspector shows its input mapping, retry policy, and routing branches.

items.name: Scheduler
items.body: Triggers, upcoming runs, and a node timeline for every execution, including the ones that resumed.
items.lead: The Scheduler is the operations view for workflows that run without you: triggers, upcoming fires, run history, and the exact state of every node.

points.name: Four trigger kinds
points.body: Cron, webhook, file changes, and sensors. Overlap policy and deduplication are handled before a run is even created.

points.name: Matrix and Gantt
points.body: Every run is a column of node states. Expand one to see a Gantt of how long each node took and where it is waiting.

points.name: Run dossier
points.body: Pinned version, entry payload, pinned references, and a timeline. Replay a failed run from the failed node without re-running what already succeeded.

shots.name: scheduler-overview
shots.caption: Overview: running, waiting, failed in the last 24 hours, next fire, and the approvals waiting on you.

items.name: Notifications
items.body: A durable ledger of approvals, completions, and failures, plus native OS notifications.
items.lead: Anything that needs you, and anything you should know, is written to a durable ledger and mirrored to native OS notifications.

points.name: Needs you first
points.body: Approval requests are grouped at the top with the rendered content and Approve and Reject actions.

points.name: Every outcome, one place
points.body: Run completions, failures, environment repairs, key checks, and MCP mount warnings, each with a link to where it happened.

points.name: Nothing transient
points.body: The ledger is the record. The top band and OS notifications are just the fast path to it.

shots.name: notifications
shots.caption: The ledger with an approval waiting, rendered from the workflow's approval node.

items.name: Library
items.body: Documents and skills in a native editor, with outline, properties, and backlinks.
items.lead: Documents and skills are knowledge the AI can read and write. Workflows file documents here, agents read them, and you edit them in a native editor.

points.name: A real document tree
points.body: Folders, pages, tags, descriptions, and properties. Wikilinks between pages produce backlinks automatically.

points.name: Written by workflows, edited by you
points.body: The digest a workflow produced is a normal page: outline, headings, lists, and code blocks.

points.name: Skills
points.body: Reusable instruction bundles with files and allowed tools that agents can mount.

shots.name: library
shots.caption: The weekly digest filed by the workflow, with its outline, properties, and two backlinks.

shots.name: library-onboarding
shots.caption: The Onboarding page: checklist, wikilinks to other pages, inline code, and a code block, all in the native editor.

items.name: Settings
items.body: Models and keys, MCP servers, storage, network, and shortcuts. Managed by default, BYOK when you want it.
items.lead: Managed models work out of the box. Add your own provider keys, choose a model per scenario, mount MCP servers, and manage local storage and sandboxes.

points.name: Managed by default
points.body: A free managed tier is provisioned on first launch with no key setup. Quota and reset date are visible at a glance.

points.name: Bring your own keys
points.body: OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen, and more. Keys are encrypted locally. Each scenario, from dialogue to image generation, picks its own model.

points.name: Everything local
points.body: Data directory, database and attachment sizes, retention, sandbox runtimes, and network settings are all on your machine.

shots.name: settings
shots.caption: Models and keys: the managed tier, three BYOK keys, and per-scenario default models.

how.title: From a Conversation to a Running Workflow.
how.lead: This is the full path of one request, using real screens from the app. The request: every Monday at 09:00, collect the last two weeks of GitHub activity, write a digest, wait for approval, and file it in the Library.

steps.name: 1 · Describe the outcome
steps.body: You write one message. Anselm plans the work as a checklist, then creates each building block in order, reporting every tool call as a card you can open.

steps.name: 2 · The workflow exists
steps.body: A cron trigger, three parallel GitHub fetches, an Agent that writes the digest, a Control node that skips empty weeks, an approval node, a Function that files the document, and a Handler that announces it. Open the graph editor and every node shows its input mapping and retry policy; control nodes also show their routing branches.

steps.name: 3 · A run fails, then gets fixed
steps.body: An earlier run failed at fetch_commits with a 502 from GitHub. Anselm added retry with backoff to the Function, published version 2, and every later run used it. All runs stay in the matrix, including the failed one.

steps.name: 4 · A run waits for you
steps.body: The latest run collected 32 commits, wrote the digest, and parked at the approval node. The Gantt shows exactly where time went.

steps.name: 5 · Approve from the ledger
steps.body: The approval request is rendered in the notification ledger with the digest summary and counts. Approve, and the run resumes from that node.

steps.name: 6 · The draft is ready to publish
steps.body: The draft is already in Weekly digests, tagged draft, with an outline and backlinks. Approval publishes it. Next Monday the cron fires on its own.

durablePage.title: Built for Unattended Execution.
durablePage.lead: This page covers the execution model behind every scheduled run. Anselm records each node result, pins versions for in-flight runs, pauses for human approval when a step needs it, and picks up exactly where it stopped after a restart.

topics.name: Completed steps never run twice
topics.body: Each node result is written to the database as it completes. On recovery the interpreter re-walks the graph, reuses completed nodes, and only executes what has not run. External side effects are never repeated.

topics.name: Pinned versions
topics.body: A run pins the workflow version and every referenced entity version when it starts. Editing an Agent or Function never changes a run that is already in flight.

topics.name: Human in the loop
topics.body: Approval nodes park the run as a persistent state. A person decides from the ledger or the Scheduler, or a timeout policy decides for them. Either way the run continues from that node.

topics.name: Observable by design
topics.body: Every run has a matrix column, a Gantt, a dossier with entry payload and pinned references, and an activity log of what each Function, Handler, and Agent did.

durable.title: Built for Unattended Execution.
durable.body: Workflows that run while you are away need more than retries. Anselm records every node result, pins versions for in-flight runs, pauses for human approval when a step needs it, and picks up exactly where it stopped after a restart.

points.name: Completed steps never run twice
points.body: Completed nodes are reused on recovery. External side effects are not repeated.

points.name: Pinned versions
points.body: Editing an entity never changes a run that is already in flight.

points.name: Human in the loop
points.body: Approval nodes park the run and wait for a decision or a timeout policy.

points.name: Inspectable
points.body: Every run has a node timeline, inputs, outputs, and the exact versions it used.

deployment.title: Local-First. Your Data Stays on Your Machine.
deployment.body: Anselm runs as a desktop app with all data in local SQLite and files. Use managed models through the Anselm API with no key setup, or bring your own provider keys.

service.title: Official service domain.
service.lead: anselm.website is the official domain of the Anselm desktop application. The managed API used by the app is hosted at api.anselm.website.

sections.name: Scope
sections.body: This domain operates the Anselm application service and this website. The API is not an open proxy, a public relay, or a general-purpose AI gateway. Access is rate-limited and intended for Anselm clients only.

sections.name: Hosts
sections.body: anselm.website serves this website. api.anselm.website serves the managed model and media API used by the desktop app. No other host under this domain is a public service.

sections.name: Contact
sections.body: For security, abuse, or operational concerns, contact the operator through the project repository on GitHub or the repository owner.
